brief: A tool caddy with a carry handle and divided bins for screws and bits.

requirements.evidence: Three full cells (pieces at q -1, 0, 1), with the open faces capped and the joints bolted together.
handle:0,0,0;top sits on cover:0,0,0;full;top over the middle cell, so the caddy can be carried from the centre. The configurator didn't check how much weight it can carry.
bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 has 3 compartments, shown with M3 screws, nuts and standoffs.
bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 has 2 compartments for bits. There is no bit prop, so for display they hold M3 screws and M3 nuts.

finish.summary: I built a tool caddy from three hex cells in a row. The middle cell has a top cover with a carry handle on it. The left cell holds a full-depth bin with 3 compartments and the right cell a full-depth bin with 2 compartments. All open faces are capped and the joints between the cells are bolted. check_build found no rule errors and the mesh-collision check came back clear. The catalog has no screwdriver-bit prop, and the drivers and hex keys I tried didn't fit in the compartments. So for the display, all five compartments hold small M3 parts (screws, nuts, standoffs); in real use the right-hand bin is meant for bits. Seen from above, every prop is at least partly visible, though they sit below the bin rims from the side. The configurator checks fit only, so it can't tell me how much load the handle will carry.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
